gears.spur_geometry.title: Spur gear module, circular pitch and pitch diameter (metric)

variables.name: p
variables.desc: circular pitch (arc length between adjacent teeth on the pitch circle)

assumptions: Metric (module) system. Circular pitch p = pi m. For the imperial diametral-pitch system see diametral_pitch (m in mm = 25.4 / P_d).

gears.diametral_pitch.title: Diametral pitch (imperial, teeth per unit length)
assumptions: P_d = N/d. The conventional diametral pitch in teeth/inch = P_d x 0.0254 (so d = 2.5 in and N = 20 give 8 teeth/inch). Module m (mm) = 25.4 / P_d(in^-1).

gears.tooth_proportions.title: Standard full-depth tooth proportions (addendum, dedendum, clearance)

variables.name: a
variables.desc: addendum (radial tooth height above the pitch circle)

variables.name: b
variables.desc: dedendum (radial depth below the pitch circle)

assumptions: Standard 20 deg full-depth involute proportions: addendum = m, dedendum = 1.25 m, clearance = 0.25 m. Stub and other systems use different coefficients.

gears.center_distance.title: Center distance and pitch diameters of a gear pair
assumptions: Standard centers (no profile shift): C = (d1 + d2)/2 = m(N1 + N2)/2.

gears.gear_ratio.title: Gear ratio, speed ratio and torque ratio
assumptions: Ideal (100% efficiency) single mesh: power is conserved, T1 omega1 = T2 omega2, so T2 = i T1. Multiply by an efficiency for real losses. i > 1 is a speed reducer. i is a MAGNITUDE (|N2/N1|); the signed train value with direction (external vs internal mesh) is carried by mechanisms.gear_pair.
method_references: Speed/torque ratio of a gear pair (recalled)

gears.contact_ratio.title: Contact ratio of a standard spur gear pair

variables.name: m_c
variables.desc: contact ratio (mean number of teeth in contact)

assumptions: Standard full-depth 20 deg involute (addendum = m). m_c = path of contact / base pitch. Requires m_c > 1.2 for smooth running; addendum modification (profile shift) changes it.
method_references: Length of path of contact / base pitch (AGMA geometry; recalled)

gears.min_teeth_interference.title: Minimum teeth to avoid interference (with a rack / large gear)

variables.name: k
variables.desc: addendum factor (addendum/module; 1 for standard full depth)

assumptions: N_min = 2k/sin^2(phi) is the smallest tooth count on a gear meshing with a rack (or a very large gear) that avoids undercut. Standard 20 deg full-depth: N_min = 17.1, so use >= 17 (18 recommended). Profile shift allows fewer teeth.
method_references: Minimum teeth to avoid interference N_min = 2k/sin^2(phi) (recalled)

gears.min_teeth_pinion.title: Minimum pinion teeth to avoid interference with a mating gear (ratio m_G)

variables.name: N_P
variables.desc: minimum pinion teeth to avoid interference with the gear

variables.name: k
variables.desc: addendum factor (addendum/module; 1 for standard full depth)

variables.name: m_G
variables.desc: gear ratio N_G/N_P (mating gear teeth / pinion teeth)

assumptions: Minimum pinion teeth to avoid interference (undercut) when meshing with a gear of ratio m_G = N_G/N_P. Reduces to the rack limit N_min = 2k/sin^2(phi) as m_G -> inf. Standard 20 deg full-depth, m_G = 2: N_P = 14.16 (use 15+). Profile shift allows fewer teeth.
method_references: Minimum pinion teeth to avoid interference with a mating gear (recalled)

gears.spur_tooth_forces.title: Spur gear tooth forces: tangential and radial (separating)

variables.name: T
variables.desc: torque on the gear being analysed

assumptions: Spur gears carry no axial load (W_a = 0). W_t is tangential at the pitch point; use the pitch diameter (AGMA uses the operating pitch diameter).
method_references: Tangential tooth load W_t = 2T/d; W_r = W_t tan(phi) (recalled)

gears.helical_pitch.title: Helical gear normal/transverse pitches, modules and pitch diameter
assumptions: Helical gears are cut in the normal plane, so m_n (and p_n) are the standard values. Transverse quantities are the axial-projected ones: m_t = m_n/cos(psi), p_t = p_n/cos(psi), d = m_t N.

gears.helical_angles.title: Helical gear transverse pressure angle from normal pressure angle
assumptions: tan(phi_t) = tan(phi_n)/cos(psi). phi_t > phi_n for helical gears.
method_references: Transverse pressure angle of a helical gear (recalled)

gears.helical_tooth_forces.title: Helical gear tooth forces: tangential, radial and axial thrust

variables.name: T
variables.desc: torque on the gear being analysed

assumptions: W_a = W_t tan(psi) is the axial thrust the helix produces (use thrust bearings). W_r uses the normal pressure angle resolved through the helix.

gears.bevel_angles.title: Bevel gear pitch cone angles (shaft angle Sigma)
assumptions: Straight/spiral bevel gears. For the common right-angle case (Sigma = 90 deg): tan(gamma1) = N1/N2, tan(gamma2) = N2/N1 and gamma1 + gamma2 = Sigma.

gears.bevel_forces.title: Bevel gear tooth forces: tangential, radial and axial

variables.name: W_t
variables.desc: transmitted (tangential) tooth force at the mean radius

variables.name: T
variables.desc: torque on the gear being analysed

variables.name: d_m
variables.desc: mean pitch diameter of that gear

variables.name: gamma
variables.desc: pitch cone angle of that gear
variables.label: γ

assumptions: Forces at the mean radius of the bevel gear. The radial/axial split depends on the pitch cone angle gamma: the axial component is W_t tan(phi) sin(gamma).

gears.worm_geometry.title: Worm lead, lead angle and axial pitch
assumptions: Lead L_w = axial pitch x number of starts; tan(lambda) = L_w/(pi d_w).

gears.worm_efficiency.title: Worm gear efficiency (worm driving)

variables.name: f
variables.desc: coefficient of friction at the mesh

assumptions: Worm driving the gear. If the gear tries to drive the worm (reversal) the efficiency is (cos(phi_n) - f/tan(lam))/(cos(phi_n) + f*tan(lam)); the worm is self-locking when f >= cos(phi_n)*tan(lam) (the normal pressure angle reduces the effective lead-angle tangent; the bare f >= tan(lam) overstates the locking limit).

gears.worm_heat.title: Worm gear power loss and heat dissipation capacity

variables.name: H_loss
variables.desc: power lost to heat (1 - eta) P_in

variables.name: H_diss
variables.desc: housing heat-dissipation capacity h A dT

variables.name: h
variables.desc: overall heat-transfer coefficient of the housing (input)

variables.name: dT
variables.desc: allowable temperature rise (delta, K = degC difference)

assumptions: Worm drives are usually limited by heat, not strength: require H_diss >= H_loss. h is an input (h ~ 10-15 W/m^2/K for still air, higher with a fan on the worm shaft).

gears.planetary_torques.title: Planetary gear torques (ideal, lossless)
assumptions: Ideal lossless train: T_S + T_R + T_C = 0, T_R = R T_S, T_C = -(1 + R) T_S. The carrier carries the largest (reaction) torque. Multiply by efficiency for losses. Speeds (the Willis relation omega_S - omega_C = -(Z_R/Z_S)(omega_R - omega_C)) are owned by mechanisms.planetary_trains; this calculator gives only the torques that follow from power balance.

gears.lewis_bending.title: Lewis bending stress (sigma = W_t / (F m Y))

variables.name: Y
variables.desc: Lewis form factor (module/diametral-pitch based; table/input for the tooth count)

assumptions: Static Lewis stress. Y is the Lewis form factor for the standard full-depth tooth, based on the module (SI) / diametral-pitch (imperial) system and read from a table for the tooth count (input). For a moving tooth the dynamic stress MULTIPLIES by the Barth velocity factor Kv (>= 1): sigma = Kv Wt/(F m Y), consistent with the AGMA Kv (see barth_velocity_factor). Compare with the material allowable bending stress.
method_references: Lewis bending equation sigma = W_t/(F m Y) (recalled)

gears.barth_velocity_factor.title: Barth velocity (dynamic) factor Kv (multiplying form, Kv >= 1)

variables.name: Kv_cast
variables.desc: Kv for cast-iron / cast teeth = (3.05 + V)/3.05

procedure.python:
def _barth(values):
    """Barth velocity factor Kv (multiplying form, Kv >= 1) for the Lewis bending path, V in m/s.

    Kv_cast   = (3.05 + V)/3.05        cast-iron / cast teeth
    Kv_cut    = (6.1 + V)/6.1          cut or milled teeth
    Kv_hobbed = (3.56 + sqrt(V))/3.56  hobbed or shaped teeth
    Kv_shaved = (5.56 + sqrt(V))/5.56  shaved or ground teeth
    The additive constants carry units of m/s (sqrt(V) terms carry sqrt(m/s)), so this is a procedure
    (not a dimensional equation). Kv >= 1 multiplies the static Lewis stress: sigma = Kv Wt/(F m Y).
    """
    V = values['V']
    sv = math.sqrt(V)
    return {'Kv_cast': (3.05 + V) / 3.05,
            'Kv_cut': (6.1 + V) / 6.1,
            'Kv_hobbed': (3.56 + sv) / 3.56,
            'Kv_shaved': (5.56 + sv) / 5.56}

assumptions: Barth empirical velocity factor in MULTIPLYING form Kv >= 1, V in m/s. The additive constants (3.05, 6.1, 3.56, 5.56 m/s) are empirical; the sqrt(V) forms apply to the hobbed/shaped and shaved/ground accuracy classes. Use Kv with the static Lewis stress as sigma = Kv Wt/(F m Y); the AGMA quality-number Kv (an input to agma_bending) is a different dynamic factor.

gears.agma_bending.title: AGMA bending stress (all modifying factors)

variables.name: J
variables.desc: geometry factor for bending strength (AGMA figure)

assumptions: AGMA 2001-C95/2101-D04 bending stress (SI form). All modifying factors Ko/Kv/Ks/Km/KB and the geometry factor J are INPUTS naming the AGMA tables/figures. Feed the result to gear_safety_factors.

gears.agma_contact.title: AGMA contact (pitting) stress (all modifying factors)

variables.name: Cp
variables.desc: elastic coefficient (AGMA table; e.g. 191 MPa^0.5 steel/steel)

variables.name: I
variables.desc: geometry factor for pitting resistance (AGMA figure)

assumptions: AGMA 2101-D04 contact (pitting) stress (SI form), sigma_c = Cp sqrt(Wt Ko Kv Ks Km Cf /(d_p F I)). Cp, Cf, all modifying factors and the geometry factor I are INPUTS naming the AGMA tables/figures.

gears.gear_safety_factors.title: Gear safety factors against bending and pitting

variables.name: n_b
variables.desc: factor of safety against bending fatigue

variables.name: CH
variables.desc: hardness-ratio factor (AGMA table; = 1 for equal hardness)

assumptions: S_t, S_c, YN, ZN, CH, KT, KR are INPUTS naming the AGMA material/figures/tables. n_b is the bending factor of safety S_F, compared directly (stress-linear). n_c is S_H, a strength/stress ratio: pitting is a Hertzian (stress-squared) failure, so the pitting factor of safety is S_H^2 = n_c^2 — compare S_F with S_H^2, not with S_H. n_b, n_c >= 1 (design codes apply larger minimums).

gears.gear_life_cycles.title: Gear life: number of load cycles from hours at speed

variables.name: n
variables.desc: shaft speed in rev/s (enter rpm/60 or "1/min")

assumptions: N = L_h * 3600 * n revolutions of that shaft; each tooth of that gear sees one load application per revolution in a single mesh. For a gear with several meshes per revolution (idler, planet) multiply by the number of meshes. Use the pinion speed for the pinion tooth and the gear speed for the gear tooth; feed N into the stress-cycle factors YN/ZN (inputs).

All >= 1 and decrease toward 1 as V -> 0.
